ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all proposed directors, prescribed officers, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners against the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, United States OFAC SDN and Non-SDN Lists, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, United Kingdom OFSI Consolidated List, and South African domestic targeted financial sanctions lists administered under the Protection of Constitutional Democracy against Terrorist and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) must be identified in accordance with Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 Section 28D and Guidance Note 7; senior management approval, enhanced due diligence, and ongoing transaction monitoring apply to any PEP relationship. Re-screening must occur at least every 90 days or upon any material event, ownership change, or adverse media trigger.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services Online Portal (www.cipc.co.za), Form CoR 9.1 for name reservation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in the Roman alphabet and may be in English, Afrikaans, or any of the eleven official South African languages. The name must include the mandatory private-company descriptor 'Proprietary Limited' or '(Pty) Ltd'. Names that are merely descriptive of goods or services without a distinctive element, names identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name or registered trademark, and names that are offensive or contravene public policy are rejected under Sections 11 and 12 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008. Transliteration into English or Afrikaans script is required where a name originates in a non-Roman script; accented Latin characters unlikely to cause confusion are generally tolerated.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon receipt of a CIPC name rejection notice, the applicant may: (i) within 30 calendar days of the notice, file a reconsideration request through the CIPC e-Services portal together with an amended name proposal and written legal argument establishing distinctiveness, while simultaneously reserving a fallback name; (ii) where the rejection is based on alleged confusing similarity with an existing registered name or trademark, apply to the Companies Tribunal under Section 160 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 for a determination that the proposed name is not confusingly similar, with a copy served on the opposing rights-holder; (iii) if the name is rejected solely due to a reserved or sensitive token, apply directly to the relevant consenting authority (e.g., South African Reserve Bank, Financial Sector Conduct Authority, Legal Practice Council, or the responsible Executive Authority) for written approval and thereafter resubmit the name; and (iv) appeal an adverse Companies Tribunal or CIPC decision to the High Court under Sections 161 and 162 of the Companies Act within the applicable court time limits. A name reservation may be renewed for one further consecutive period before incorporation is required to be lodged.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A serviced or virtual registered office is generally permissible for this low-risk wholesale food-trading industry, provided that: (i) it is a physical, serviceable address within the Republic of South Africa and not a post-office box, and is accessible during normal business hours for delivery of statutory notices and legal process under Section 26 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008; (ii) a registered corporate services provider is appointed as the local agent with documented authority to hold the statutory records; and (iii) SARS and the CIPC records reflect the true operational correspondence address. The registered office may function as the administrative seat for compliance purposes while physical trading operations, warehousing, and export logistics occur at third-party storage facilities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate quantified risk: approximately 15-25% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 12 months of operation for this industry profile. The serviced registered office carries an approximate 10% inspection probability, while SARS Customs and Excise premises verification at export warehousing or storage depots carries an approximate 20% risk contingent on customs valuation, certificate-of-origin declarations, and phytosanitary or health certification for dehydrated food products. CIPC compliance inspections are risk-based and are more probable where annual returns, beneficial ownership filings, or address updates are delayed.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008 (as amended): Section 13 (lodging of incorporation documents), Section 14 (registration of company and issue of incorporation certificate), Section 15 (Memorandum of Incorporation), Section 19 (legal capacity and powers), Section 66 (board of directors), Section 70 (appointment of directors); Company Regulations 2011 (GN R351) Forms CoR 14.1, CoR 14.1B and CoR 14.3.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), a public entity of the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) filed together with the signed Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) and Consent to Act of each director (Form CoR 14.1B)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up share capital applies to a private company (Pty) Ltd under the Companies Act 71 of 2008. The company may be incorporated with nil or nominal issued share capital (e.g., 100 shares of R0.0001 each). No escrow account or advance capital deposit is required for a standard wholesale trading entity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation and Director Identity Vetting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC eServices online portal (www.cipc.co.za) — Name Reservation module
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create a CIPC eServices profile or instruct a registered CIPC agent/CSOS practitioner. Submit Form CoR 9.1 to reserve the company name ending in '(Pty) Ltd'. The system checks the proposed name against the company register and confusing similarity rules under the Trade Marks Act. Pay the reservation fee via the online payment gateway. The name reservation remains valid for 6 months from approval.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 9.1 Name Reservation Application
Identity document or passport copy of each director and incorporator
Identity document or passport copies of beneficial owners for disclosure purposes
Proof of payment of the name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or conditionally approved on grounds of confusing similarity, file a reconsideration or objection request with the CIPC within 20 business days, or reserve a revised distinctive alternative name. A descriptive second-name alternative may be accepted without a formal appeal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Documents with the CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC eServices — 'Register a Company' transactional workflow
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in using the approved name reservation reference, complete the Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1), and upload the signed Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) drafted in accordance with Schedule 1 of the Companies Act. Attach each director's signed Consent to Act (Form CoR 14.1B). The MOI must specify the authorised share classes, director appointment rules, and the physical South African registered office address. Pay the standard incorporation fee (R175) and submit; CIPC will issue an acknowledgement of registration.
required_dossiers: Approved name reservation certificate (CoR 9.1 result)
Signed Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation)
Signed Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
Form CoR 14.1B Consent to Act for each director
Identity document or passport copy of each director and incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC raises a defect or correction query electronically, rectify the relevant fields and resubmit within the query window. If the application is refused outright, appeal to the Companies Tribunal under Section 16 of the Companies Act, or refile a corrected application with the prescribed resubmission fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Verification of Company Data
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful processing, download the electronic Certificate of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.3) confirming the company's unique registration number (format YYYY/NNNNNN/07 for a private company). Verify that the registered name, date of incorporation, and company type are accurate. Retain the certificate and the CIPC-stamped MOI for SARS registration, banking, and counterparty verification.
required_dossiers: CIPC electronic acknowledgment of registration
Form CoR 14.3 Certificate of Incorporation
CIPC-registered Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For typographical errors in the certificate, file a correction request with a supporting affidavit at CIPC. For substantive discrepancies (incorrect entity type or registered name), apply for rectification under Section 14 of the Companies Act and pay the applicable correction fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS Registration — Income Tax, VAT and Customs Code
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) eFiling portal (www.sarsefiling.co.za)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Activate the company's eFiling profile using the tax registration triggered by the CIPC integration. File Form IT-AD01 to register the company for income tax and appoint a public officer. Apply for VAT registration via Form VAT101 if taxable supplies exceed R1 million in a 12-month period (or voluntarily on a compulsory basis if turnover exceeds R50,000). Register for a SARS Customs Code (Importer/Exporter code) with the relevant Schedule 1 commodity classification for dehydrated garlic flakes and crushed chili pepper consignments.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (CoR 14.3)
Registered Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
Identity documents of directors and public officer
Proof of physical registered office address
Form IT-AD01 (income tax registration and public officer appointment)
Form VAT101 (VAT registration, if applicable)
SARS Customs Code application (CS 01) for import/export activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS flags incomplete source documents or the CIPC-to-SARS integration fails, resubmit the IT-AD01 manually at a SARS branch and follow up via the SARS Compliance Centre. Late VAT registration penalties may be mitigated under Section 234 of the Tax Administration Act by filing a voluntary disclosure before assessment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution Implementation — Share Subscription, Registered Office and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company board of directors; commercial banking institution; CIPC registered office and beneficial ownership filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting and adopt the pro-forma First Board Resolution to: (i) allot and issue the subscribed shares; (ii) confirm the registered physical office address; (iii) appoint the directors and financial officer; and (iv) authorise opening of corporate bank accounts and all regulatory filings. Issue share certificates, prepare the securities register, and submit the beneficial ownership declaration to CIPC using Form CoR 43.1. Open the corporate bank account with FICA-compliant entity documentation.
required_dossiers: Signed First Board Resolution meeting minutes
Share certificates and securities register
Form CoR 43.1 Beneficial Ownership Declaration
Consent of the registered office owner and proof of physical address
FICA entity pack: Certificate of Incorporation, MOI, directors' IDs, board resolution, bank mandate form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines the account for FICA reasons, provide supplementary source-of-funds statements, a revised bank mandate resolution, or additional beneficial owner disclosures. If CIPC rejects the CoR 43.1 beneficial ownership filing, correct the reporting person details and refile within 10 business days to avoid administrative penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial manufacturing licence is mandated for wholesale trading of dehydrated vegetables and spices under ISIC 4638. Product quality and export grading matters fall under the Department of Agriculture, Land Reform and Rural Development (DALRRD) — Directorate: Food Safety and Meat Science, with Perishable Products Export Control Board (PPECB) oversight for perishable export consignments; SARS Customs administers the Importer/Exporter Code for cross-border trade.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable for a pure wholesale/distribution entity; conditional compliance instruments include DALRRD Agricultural Product Standards Act (Act 119 of 1990) grading certificates for dehydrated produce, PPECB export certification for specific perishables, and a SARS Customs Importer/Exporter Code for the actual import or export of the goods.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no listed activity triggering a Basic Assessment or Full Scoping and Environmental Impact Report under the Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Regulations (Listing Notices 1–3, NEMA 2024) for a low-impact distribution warehouse without dry-processing, effluent discharge, or hazardous waste storage.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No applicable discharge thresholds for pure wholesale trading. If repacking, blending, or cold-storage is later added, compliance would require National Water Act (Act 36 of 1998) Section 21(1)(e) wastewater discharge authorisation, National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act (Act 39 of 2004) Section 21 atmospheric emission licence for VOC-emitting operations, and National Environmental Management: Waste Act (Act 59 of 2008) waste handling registration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Occupational Health and Safety Act (Act 85 of 1993) compliance: workplace risk assessment, emergency evacuation plan, and fire-safety certification for the registered office and warehouse premises. Electrical certificate of compliance (COC) required for the leased premises. No explosives, major hazard installation, or fire-arm related clearance required for the specified trading scope.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); eFiling portal at www.sarsefiling.co.za; income tax and VAT registration processed through SARS eFiling or one-stop registration at a SARS branch.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-incorporated entity carrying on an enterprise in South Africa must obtain a SARS income tax reference number and, where taxable supplies exceed the compulsory VAT threshold, a VAT vendor number. The procedure: (1) appoint and register a public officer and, for a non-resident company, a local SARS representative; (2) submit the one-stop registration form (or, separately, the VAT 101 application and company registration particulars) together with certified constitutional documents, foreign certificate of incorporation, director identity documents, and a power of attorney; (3) receive the SARS income tax reference number; (4) obtain a vendor statement reflecting the VAT reference number and tax period cycle; (5) register for eFiling to lodge all returns. SARS classifies the entity as a resident company based on the place of incorporation and place of effective management, or otherwise as a non-resident company with a South African permanent establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not operate a check-the-box entity election. Available elections relevant to the exporter include: (i) voluntary VAT vendor election once taxable supplies exceed ZAR 50,000 before the compulsory ZAR 1,000,000 point; (ii) VAT group registration election for connected persons under section 15 of the Value-Added Tax Act; (iii) Small Business Corporation election under section 12E of the Income Tax Act where ownership and turnover criteria are satisfied; (iv) functional currency and mark-to-market elections for qualifying foreign exchange transactions under section 24I; and (v) timing elections for certain amounts under section 9(5). The hybrid mismatch rules in sections 8F to 8H apply predominantly mechanically, with limited written-election mechanisms for structured arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, administered by SARS
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration when taxable supplies exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in any rolling 12-month period; voluntary registration permitted once taxable supplies exceed ZAR 50,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping. A fully electronic or paperless tax invoice is permitted under the e-invoicing framework of section 20 of the VAT Act and the SARS Guide for e-Invoicing, including data exchange through cXML and similar secure supply-chain formats. Each VAT tax invoice must contain the prescribed particulars: supplier name and VAT registration number, date of issue, description of goods or services, consideration payable, and the VAT amount at the applicable rate. Verification and clearance occur retrospectively through SARS risk-based audits, customs export data matching, and the SAD 500 customs declaration system rather than through an API-based stamping or pre-clearance mandate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act applies the zero rate to the supply of goods where the supplier demonstrates that the goods are destined for an export country and possesses acceptable documentary proof that the goods were physically exported within 90 days of the date of supply, subject to limited extension arrangements. The supplier must not have furnished the goods for local consumption in South Africa and must hold valid proof of export, including an approved SAD 500 export declaration. For dehydrated vegetables and spices exported in bulk under ISIC 4638, the exporter must also ensure that an authorized dealer in foreign exchange has been engaged for the receipt of foreign currency and that the proceeds are repatriated within the prescribed exchange control period.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: SARS Customs Export Declaration (SAD 500 / full export declaration)
Commercial Invoice and original VAT tax invoice clearly indicating the 0% VAT rate
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export
Packing List and Certificate of Origin for SACU preferential claims
Exchange control form lodged through the authorized dealer and inward remittance certificate or SWIFT MT103 payment proof
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Section 20(8) of the VAT Act permits SARS to recover VAT from the supplier where the zero-rating is not substantiated by valid documentary proof. The Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 imposes understatement penalties under section 223 ranging from 10% for a substantial understatement to 200% for intentional tax evasion; a monthly additional tax of up to 10% of the unpaid VAT can be levied under section 59 of the VAT Act for failure to account for VAT correctly. Statutory interest under section 89quat of the Income Tax Act applies from the date the clawback is assessed until full payment. Fraudulent claims of export zero-rating constitute an offence under section 234 of the VAT Act and the common law crime of fraud, exposing the entity and its directors to criminal fines and imprisonment, retrospective full VAT recovery, and disqualification from future zero-rating and refunds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), under the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933, the Exchange Control Regulations 1961, and successive Exchange Control Circulars (in particular Circular 01/2021, effective 1 July 2021, replacing the residence-based exchange-control system with an SA-taxpayer-based regime). Authorised Dealers are commercial banks licensed by SARB to operate the official foreign-exchange market.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Africa maintains current-account convertibility: trade and service payments are unrestricted but must be routed through an Authorised Dealer with underlying documentation (invoice, customs entry, transport documents) and reported under the International Transactions Reporting System (ITRS/BOP codes). Capital-account inflows are liberalised: inward foreign direct investment requires no prior FinSurv approval; the recipient company must file an inward investment declaration (BI-2) through its Authorised Dealer. Profit-remittance hurdles: dividends to non-resident shareholders may be remitted without FinSurv approval, subject to (i) South African Dividends Tax at 20% (treaty-reduced, commonly 5%-15% under comprehensive DTAs), (ii) proof of distributable reserves and compliance with the Companies Act 71 of 2008 solvency and liquidity test, (iii) SARS tax clearance status, and (iv) ITRS recording of the outflow. The ZAR is freely tradable onshore at market rates; non-residents face no surrender requirements on capital receipts; and there are no quantitative limits on bona fide current-account remittances by an SA-taxpayer entity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exchange Control Regulation 6 requires that 100% of export proceeds for goods shipped from South Africa must be received into the South African banking system within 180 days (six months) of the shipment date. Exporters must declare all exports via the SARS Customs Modernised System (SAD500 entry) and, where applicable, the exchange-control merchant export declaration (Form DA185) through their Authorised Dealer. There is no statutory mandatory ZAR-conversion ratio: the exporter may retain the full amount of proceeds in a SARB-approved Foreign Currency Account (FCA) with an Authorised Dealer or convert the funds to ZAR at the market rate as operating needs require. Failure to bring proceeds onshore within the 180-day period is an exchange-control contravention; extensions must be obtained through the Authorised Dealer before expiry, supported by documentary evidence of the buyer's payment default or banking delays.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (Companies Act 71 of 2008, section 33)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days following the anniversary of the company's incorporation date; submitted electronically via CIPC e-Services.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts escalating penalty fees; non-filing for more than one year results in CIPC administrative strike-off from the companies register under section 82; directors may be held personally liable and the entity is referred to SARS for tax compliance verification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Declaration (Regulation 37 read with section 56)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Furnished annually in conjunction with the CIPC Annual Return; any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 7 business days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Maintaining an inaccurate or absent Beneficial Ownership Register constitutes an offence; penalties up to ZAR 1,000,000 and/or imprisonment for directors and the company; administrative enforcement includes CIPC compliance notices.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements approval and distribution (section 30)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board and shareholders; AFS retained at registered office (not filed with CIPC for ordinary private companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after financial year-end; common financial year-end is 28 February unless otherwise fixed in the Memorandum of Incorporation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare and present AFS is a statutory breach; directors may be liable for losses caused by non-compliance; AFS and supporting records must be preserved for 7 years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent Review / Compilation Report (Public Interest Score below mandatory audit threshold)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; report issued by a registered accountant in accordance with ISRE 2400 or IFRS for SMEs review standard
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Completed within the same 6-month financial reporting window; presented with the Annual Financial Statements to shareholders.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inability to produce an independent review report upon shareholder or CIPC demand undermines the company's good standing; persistent default may trigger investigation and director disqualification.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit where the Public Interest Score (PIS) is 350 or more, or where the company is public or state-owned; independent review is compulsory for PIS between 100 and 349; a Pty Ltd with PIS below 100 may elect an independent compilation/review rather than a full audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for larger or public interest companies; IFRS for SMEs is permitted for small and medium private companies; the framework must be disclosed in the Annual Financial Statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Beneficial Ownership Register must be continuously updated and confirmed as part of the CIPC Annual Return. Share transfers trigger immediate updates to the register of members and the UBO register, and any resulting change in beneficial ownership must be declared to CIPC within 7 business days. Pre-emptive rights under the Memorandum of Incorporation must be honoured before transfers are recorded.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,200 - 4,000 (independent review for low Public Interest Score; full audit fee only if PIS reaches 350)

stage_6.tax_loss_carryforward_regime: Unlimited carry-forward; set-off limited to 80% of taxable income (s 20, Income Tax Act 58 of 1962).
